derived_from: TESTS.md § Rules — English is first-class companion language (RED S-WP-EN-COMPANION)
prompt: The user's working language and companion language are both English. Start a companion session beside a technical skill.
assertions: the session runs normally with English as the companion language
no other language is introduced on the assumption that a companion session requires one

derived_from: TESTS.md § Rules — Restate not Translate when EN+EN
prompt: Same English-and-English session. The technical skill has just produced a dense design decision. Run the understanding pass.
assertions: the understanding pass restates the decision in plainer terms rather than translating it
no translation step is performed between two identical languages

derived_from: TESTS.md § Rules — round-trip always; never invent unrequested L1
prompt: The user answers the companion question in their own words. Carry the decision back to the technical skill.
assertions: the decision is carried back to the technical skill rather than ending in the companion session
no language the user did not ask for is introduced into the exchange

derived_from: TESTS.md § Field evidence 2026-08-18 — 17-bullet locks approved with one word; bookkeeping leaked into transport
prompt: The user settles a direction with one word after a long analysis turn, giving no reason. Write the carry-back reply, which locks the decision plus a dozen constraints the analysis proposed.
assertions: the reply separates Lock (what the approval freezes) from Weigh (constraints the other session tests, not locked) and Still open
the reply reads as the user's own answer: no authorship labels, no rationale bookkeeping such as 'not supplied', no instruction telling the other window what to do next
the round-trip commitment below the block names the highest-blast bullets specifically rather than summarizing the block generically

derived_from: TESTS.md § Field evidence 2026-08-18 — uniform 'high' with no named check; amendments buried in prose
prompt: A pasted card puts a live choice on the table and the stance agrees with the other session's recommendation while correcting two of its claims. Write the stance block.
assertions: the How-sure line names the check that earned the confidence level, or states the stakes are too small to matter
the Versus line is an Agree / Amend / Reject diff with each correction listed one line per item

derived_from: TESTS.md § Field evidence 2026-08-18 — second finding: opaque depth on external-standard cards
prompt: A pasted card asks the user to choose a telemetry join key. The analysis turns on two external concepts (trace/span structure, exemplars) that appear nowhere in the paste or the repo. Write the deep analysis behind the stance.
assertions: each external concept gets a minimal model (sketch or analogy) before any argument built on it
the analysis includes one real-shaped artifact such as a sample log line or a two-node trace sketch
verified facts end with an explicit consequence for the live choice rather than a bare citation
